1: Part 1: How to analyse the Baseline test

The Baseline paper (40 questions) has no **official** cutoff. Its purpose: to find which subject has a weak base. Do not label the candidate "weak/strong" from the total score alone; look at section-wise and question-wise mistakes.
Step 1: Enter the candidate's 40 answers in the "Baseline_40" sheet of the Excel tracker (A/B/C/D, blank = unanswered).
Step 2: The tracker shows section-wise score and %.
Step 3: For each wrong question decide the Error category: Conceptual / Calculation / Terminology / Careless (Error_Log sheet).
Step 4: Choose the next Paper from the mapping below.
Step 5: Teach that Paper's Remediation Notes, then a short quiz.

Part 2: Accounting Equation  A = L + C
Simple idea: whatever you have (Assets) is either other people's money (Liabilities) or your own (Capital). So **Assets = Liabilities + Capital**. After every transaction both sides remain equal.
Closing Capital = Opening Capital + Profit − Drawings (+ additional Capital)

Step 1: Capital = Assets − Liabilities

3: Part 1: What are Debit and Credit?
Debit = left side (Dr), Credit = right side (Cr). They do not mean good/bad; they are just the side of the record.
*The Bank account behaves the same way in transactions — Debit when money comes in, Credit when it goes out.

6: GST = Goods and Services Tax; an **indirect tax** on the **supply** of goods and services. The burden finally falls on the consumer; the trader only deposits it with the government.

**Rates (from 22 Sep 2025, checked on 2026-10-19):** main rates 5% and 18%; 40% on selected sin/luxury goods. The earlier 12% and 28% rates generally no longer apply. If you see 12%/28% in old notes, they are outdated.
GST paid on purchases (Input) can be deducted from GST on sales (Output) (conditions apply). This avoids tax on tax.

TDS = Tax Deducted at Source. The payer deducts tax and deposits it with the government. Rates/thresholds change with the law; **always check current rates on incometax.gov.in** (we only saw secondary sources).
Salary TDS: the employer deducts estimated annual tax ÷ 12 every month.
Income Tax is a direct tax (Central Government).
Income-tax Act, 2025 — from 1 April 2026 (the Tax Year concept).
Slab: income is split into portions, each taxed at a different rate.

Part 2: Deficits in the Government Budget
Revenue Deficit = Revenue Expenditure − Revenue Receipts
Fiscal Deficit = Total Expenditure − Total Receipts (excluding Borrowings)
Primary Deficit = Fiscal Deficit − Interest Payments
